caption:
Mountain biking in Costa Rica is rarely a matter of constant speed. The terrain here does not negotiate. On the ridges of the continental divide, old farm tracks give way to grassy passes where the grade easily climbs past twenty percent. Here, progress is measured in patience, not average pace. Pushing your bike for a hundred metres is not a defeat; it is simply the transition between two valleys, a moment to let your heart rate settle and look out over a canopy that stretches to the horizon. You trade the gears for the quiet of the highland wind. The ridge always wins the argument, but it rewards those who do not hurry the climb.
